items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (most recently 2026-06-22). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin (stopped 4/2026) and gabapentin only - no oral anticoagulant has ever been ordered in the clinic record. CHA2DS2-VASc = 9 (CHF/hypertensive heart disease with heart failure 1, hypertension 1, age 80 = 2, type 2 diabetes 1, prior cerebral infarction with residual dysarthria/hemiparesis and history of TIA 2, old myocardial infarction 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended (Class 1) oral anticoagulation is absent; aspirin is not an acceptable substitute.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) has been current since 2025-11-10 and was last reissued 2026-07-12. His most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24, the post-initiation tracing) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 549 ms and Bazett QTc 558 ms - above the 500 ms threshold and markedly longer than QTc 420 ms on 2025-06-07 before amiodarone. Most recent electrolytes: potassium 4.3 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (both 2026-06-09). Prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch list) is a current order, last reissued 2026-06-17. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 583 ms and Bazett QTc 572 ms, far above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent electrolytes: potassium 4.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 2026-06-17). She is 95 years old and also on warfarin (interaction) and metoprolol (bradycardia); prescriber review of amiodarone and a current ECG are needed.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10. The start falls between 9/1/2025 and 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (due 2025-12-10). ECG 106885519 was recorded on 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met. (That ECG showed QTc 558 ms and is the basis of a separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-02-12 (first appearance on the medication list, new order at 09:25). The start is before 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (due 2026-03-14). ECG 101538691 was recorded on 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start - within the window, so the requirement was met (QTc 455 ms, not prolonged).

Citalopram 40 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02. Because the start is on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was required within 14 days (due 2026-03-16). ECG 104882441 was obtained on 2026-03-07, 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met (QTc 390 ms).

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-04-10 (new order at 13:55). The start is after 3/1/2026, so an ECG was required within 14 days - due 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was not recorded until 2026-04-29, 19 days after the start, i.e. outside the required window, so the requirement was not met within the required time and the due date has passed.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01. An ECG was required within 14 days (due 2026-08-15). No ECG has been recorded since the start - her only tracing is 106035722 from 2025-12-25 - so the requirement is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10, so an ECG was required within 14 days (due 2026-08-24). No ECG exists in the chart for this patient, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the window - and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15. Under the revised memo an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (her last tracing is 104253928 from 2025-03-09), but the due date is after the 2026-09-24 review time, so the follow-up is not yet due.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 Dr Kessler documented a subtherapeutic INR of 1.6 and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days (due 2026-09-08). INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, within the window, so the monitoring requirement was met.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation (coded 8/2025 and carried in every cardiology clinic note, most recently 2026-06-27). Current medications are levothyroxine only; no anticoagulant appears anywhere in the clinic record. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (essential hypertension 1, age 71 = 1); coronary atherosclerosis without infarction/PAD/aortic plaque was not counted as vascular disease. A score of 2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, so the absence of therapy needs review. A single coded episode of 'hemorrhage complicating a procedure' (8/2025) is the only bleeding history and should be weighed when therapy is started.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily under the anticoagulation protocol after a home INR of 3.4. This is a dose change by a clinic pharmacist, so an INR was required within 7 days (due 2026-09-17). No INR has been resulted since 2026-06-17, so the recheck is overdue as of the 2026-09-24 review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded during the March 2025 admission for cerebral infarction due to embolism, with residual hemiparesis/facial weakness/ataxia. Cardiology clinic medication lists (most recent 2026-06-23) contain only famotidine, levothyroxine and metoprolol tartrate - no anticoagulant. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (prior cardioembolic stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 71 = 1, female 1). Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation with none current.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (most recent 2026-08-04). Current medications are famotidine, pantoprazole and sertraline - no anticoagulant, although 'long-term (current) use of anticoagulants' was coded during the June 2025 admission and inpatient warfarin was given then. CHA2DS2-VASc = 2: congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure and primary cardiomyopathy coded February 2025 (1) plus essential hypertension (1). A score of 2 in a man reaches the Class 1 threshold for oral anticoagulation, so the current absence of therapy should be reviewed.

Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was re-listed and re-ordered as a current medication at the 2026-08-20 cardiology visit even though outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. The anticoagulant is therefore being continued against a documented major bleed and an explicit hold; the indication (atrial flutter) and bleeding risk need prescriber review before it resumes. He is also on aspirin plus clopidogrel, adding to bleeding risk.

At the 2026-07-15 cardiology visit the plan was to switch the anticoagulant from rivaroxaban to apixaban, but both drugs remain on the current medication list and both were ordered at that visit: apixaban 5 mg twice daily (new order 10:05) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (continued order 10:07). Two concurrent direct oral anticoagulants (plus clopidogrel) create a serious bleeding hazard; the rivaroxaban order should have been stopped.

The cardiology note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response at about 132-136 bpm with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response, and an unspecified atrial fibrillation diagnosis was coded the same day. The documented rhythm and rate contradict the tracings and the chart needs correction.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (QT watch list) is a current order, last reissued 2026-07-15. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 504 ms and Bazett QTc 545 ms, well above the 500 ms clinic threshold. Most recent electrolytes: potassium 4.6 mEq/L (2026-07-15) and magnesium 2.0 mg/dL (2025-03-08). Citalopram 40 mg also exceeds the recommended maximum for QT safety; prescriber review of dose and a repeat ECG are needed.

Escitalopram oxalate 10 mg daily (QT watch list) is a current order, last reissued 2026-07-18. His most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT 500 ms and Bazett QTc 533 ms, above the 500 ms threshold - and up from QTc 364 ms on the previous tracing (2022-11-23). The 2024-05-14 note that started escitalopram described this ECG as 'QT acceptable', which is not supported by the tracing. Most recent electrolytes: potassium 3.8 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (both 2026-03-18).

interpretations.explanation: Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, regular; normal PR, narrow QRS, normal axis and normal QTc. Compared with the previous tracing (108651109, 2018-12-13, 66 bpm, QRS 108 ms, QTc 390 ms) the rate is slower but there is no new rhythm, conduction or QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with normal PR and QRS and normal axis, but marked QT prolongation (QT 500 ms, Bazett QTc 533 ms) - an increase of more than 60 ms from QTc 359 ms on the previous tracing (100065910, 2022-11-23). He takes escitalopram, a QT watch-list drug; a separate QT safety item has been filed.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, regular, with normal PR, QRS 98 ms and normal axis. The QT is markedly prolonged (QT 504 ms, Bazett QTc 545 ms), an increase of more than 60 ms compared with QTc 408 ms on the previous tracing (107149156, 2020-06-17). She takes citalopram 40 mg daily; a QT safety item has been filed.
Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, regular, with normal PR (132 ms), narrow QRS (76 ms), normal axis (+67 degrees) and normal QTc (413 ms). No prior ECG is available for comparison.
Sinus tachycardia at 108 bpm with a small P wave giving a PR of roughly 120 ms, QRS 92 ms, normal axis and QTc 449 ms. The tracing is noisy with baseline wander. No prior ECG for comparison.
Sinus rhythm at 98 bpm with a short PR interval (about 110 ms), narrow QRS (78 ms), axis +3 degrees and normal QTc (399 ms). No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 59 bpm with a prolonged PR of about 215 ms (first-degree AV block) and a wide QRS of 130 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL and V6 and deep wide QS complexes in V1-V3 - complete left bundle branch block. Frontal axis -21 degrees (within the normal range). QTc 449 ms, appropriate for the wide QRS. Two ventricular ectopic beats. The previous tracing (103686933, 2024-06-03) showed the same LBBB and first-degree AV block with QTc 452 ms, so there is no new change.

Irregularly irregular rhythm at about 100 bpm with no discernible P waves on any lead and beat-to-beat variation of the RR interval from 0.39 to 1.07 s - atrial fibrillation; there is also frequent ventricular ectopy. QRS is narrow (84 ms), frontal axis -49 degrees (left axis deviation) and QTc 418 ms. No PR interval is measurable. No prior ECG for comparison. This is the only tracing documenting the coded atrial fibrillation for which he takes warfarin.
Marked sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with normal PR (166 ms), QRS 94 ms, normal axis and QTc 405 ms. Comparable with the previous tracing (104629882, 58 bpm, QTc 395 ms) - no change.

Irregular rhythm at about 61 bpm with a markedly variable ventricular response (RR 0.70-1.17 s) and no consistent P wave before the QRS complexes - atrial fibrillation with a slow/moderate ventricular response. QRS 96 ms, axis +27 degrees, QTc 430 ms. The tracing three days earlier (107873952, 2024-11-12) showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with a clear P wave and PR 170 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation.

Sinus tachycardia at 122 bpm with normal PR (132 ms) and a narrow QRS (76 ms). The frontal axis is about +143 degrees (right axis deviation) with a predominantly negative QRS in lead I; the limb-lead pattern should be checked against electrode placement. QTc 404 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 01:33) showed a wide QRS of 128 ms with an rsR' pattern in V1 and terminal S waves in I and V6 - complete right bundle branch block - which is no longer present, so the bundle branch block has resolved. QTc fell from 450 to 404 ms (less than 60 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 76 bpm with a narrow QRS and normal axis; QTc 451 ms, slightly shorter than the 504 ms measured on the previous tracing (109048192, 2020-02-02) - a fall of about 50 ms, which does not reach the 60 ms threshold.
Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm with normal PR (178 ms), QRS 90 ms, normal axis (+54 degrees) and QTc 427 ms; one ventricular ectopic beat. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with a short PR interval (about 100 ms), QRS 88 ms, normal axis (+60 degrees) and QTc 420 ms. Compared with the tracing of the previous day (106045460, 62 bpm, QTc 443 ms) there is no significant change.

Sinus rhythm at about 62 bpm with isolated ventricular ectopic beats and a post-ectopic pause. PR about 195 ms (upper normal), QRS 104 ms, frontal axis about -32 degrees (borderline left axis deviation) and QTc 389 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.
Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm with normal PR (136 ms), narrow QRS (88 ms), normal axis and QTc 431 ms. Unchanged from the previous day's tracing (101016166, QTc 425 ms).
Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm with normal PR (152 ms), QRS 106 ms (upper normal, no bundle branch block pattern), normal axis (+34 degrees) and QTc 442 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus bradycardia at 55 bpm with a prolonged PR interval of about 212 ms - first-degree AV block. QRS 88 ms with tall precordial voltages, axis +4 degrees, QTc 383 ms. The previous tracing (103042067, 2024-11-30) had a PR of 184 ms and QTc 367 ms, so the PR has lengthened slightly but no listed change category applies.

Sinus tachycardia at 104 bpm with normal PR (134 ms), QRS 100 ms, normal axis (+39 degrees) and QTc 450 ms. The previous tracing (100698634, 2025-06-20) showed sinus tachycardia at 147 bpm with QTc about 413 ms; the change of roughly 40 ms does not reach the 60 ms threshold.

Sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with normal PR (148 ms), QRS 88 ms, axis -25 degrees (normal) and QTc 439 ms. Compared with the previous tracing (104232242, 2025-04-27, QTc 412 ms) the change is less than 60 ms.
Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm with normal PR (142 ms), narrow QRS (76 ms), normal axis (+53 degrees) and normal QTc (405 ms). No prior ECG for comparison.

Irregularly irregular narrow-complex tachycardia at about 150 bpm (RR 0.29-0.58 s) with no organised P waves - atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. QRS about 66 ms, axis -6 degrees, QTc 419 ms; no measurable PR interval. The tracing of the previous evening (107374881, 2025-09-12) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with PR 146 ms, so this is new atrial fibrillation. He is anticoagulated with apixaban.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, regular, with a discrete P wave before each QRS. PR is at the upper limit of normal (about 190-200 ms) but not clearly prolonged, QRS is narrow, axis normal and QTc normal. No change versus the previous tracing (106186980).
Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with normal PR (156 ms), QRS 90 ms, axis -20 degrees (normal) and QTc 390 ms. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm with a clear upright P wave in lead II, PR 162 ms, QRS 96 ms, axis +12 degrees and normal QTc (393 ms). This confirms the note of the same day describing sinus rhythm. The previous tracing two days earlier (105362569, 2025-11-21) had a QTc of 532 ms, so the QTc has fallen by more than 60 ms.

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with normal PR (170 ms) and QRS 100 ms, axis +68 degrees, but markedly prolonged repolarisation - QT 549 ms with Bazett QTc 558 ms. The previous tracing (108780865, 2025-06-07) had a QTc of 415 ms, an increase of more than 60 ms, coinciding with amiodarone started 2025-11-10. A QT safety item has been filed.
Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm with normal PR (138 ms), QRS 90 ms, axis +22 degrees and normal QTc (419 ms). No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at about 81 bpm with mild rate variation, normal PR (178 ms), narrow QRS (84 ms), normal axis (+46 degrees) and normal QTc (381 ms); one ectopic beat. This tracing confirms the 2026-03-07 note describing sinus rhythm and is the post-initiation ECG for citalopram. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with normal PR (142 ms), QRS 88 ms, normal axis (+64 degrees). Repolarisation is broad with some baseline drift; by the tangent method QT is about 425 ms giving a Bazett QTc of roughly 455 ms - borderline but below the 500 ms clinic threshold. No prior ECG for comparison.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with PR 138 ms and QRS 96 ms, QTc 388 ms. The frontal plane is unusual: the P wave, QRS and T wave are all negative in leads I and aVL with a positive QRS in lead III and a computed frontal axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation) while the precordial leads show normal R-wave progression - a pattern that should raise the possibility of left/right arm lead reversal and warrants a repeat tracing. No prior ECG for comparison.

Irregularly irregular rhythm at about 136 bpm (RR 0.35-0.65 s) with no discernible P waves - atrial fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response. QRS 98 ms, axis -1 degree, QTc 450 ms; no measurable PR interval. The earlier tracing the same day (107914094, 17:13) shows the same atrial fibrillation at about 132 bpm, so there is no change between them. Both contradict the clinic note of 2026-06-10 that recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'.
Sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm; normal PR and QRS, normal axis, QTc 419 ms. Essentially identical to the tracing taken one minute earlier the same day (102910502) - no interval change.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with clear P waves and a regular ventricular response. The QT is markedly prolonged (QT 583 ms, Bazett QTc 572 ms) in a patient on amiodarone. The previous tracing (100867733, 2022-04-06) showed atrial fibrillation with a rapid, irregular response at about 130 bpm and frequent ventricular ectopy, QTc 468 ms, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved and the QTc has increased by well over 60 ms.
Sinus tachycardia at 107 bpm with normal PR, narrow QRS, normal axis and QTc 426 ms; one ventricular ectopic beat. No change versus the previous tracing (107274479, QTc 423 ms).

Regular narrow-complex tachycardia at 141 bpm with a low-amplitude but beat-to-beat consistent P wave before each QRS - sinus tachycardia. Axis 0 degrees, QRS 78 ms, QTc 406 ms. The previous tracing two days earlier (109839112) showed irregularly irregular atrial fibrillation with no P waves, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved (rate control/cardioversion). The atrial activity is small, so an organised atrial tachycardia cannot be completely excluded.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm with a prolonged PR interval of about 215 ms - first-degree AV block; this was 138 ms on the previous tracing (102616671, 2021-05-16). QRS is narrow, axis normal at -15 degrees and QTc 416 ms (previously 398 ms), so no listed change category is met.
Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm with normal PR, narrow QRS, normal axis and normal QTc; one ectopic beat. Unchanged from the previous tracing (102955795, 115 bpm, QTc 386 ms).
